topic: How does beam steering via translational displacement impact coverage flexibility and antenna pattern stability in dynamic satellite scenarios?
consensus_response: Beam steering via translational displacement compromises coverage flexibility by introducing radiation pattern distortions caused by physical translation, particularly in LEO constellations with satellite elevation angles around 40°. This reduces angular coverage to ±40 degrees around the broadside direction. Massive beamforming technology exacerbates this issue by introducing dynamic scheduling complexities and inter-beam interference due to non-zero side lobes. Phased arrays amplify these challenges, requiring complex control systems sensitive to phase errors that can lead to reduced beam stability.
reference_context: The reference context highlights limitations of planar arrays in terms of directivity and occupied area, particularly at satellite elevation angles around 40°. Non-uniform array element spacing may mitigate radiation pattern distortions, but its impact on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and bit error rate (BER) is unclear.
